"THE WAY OF THE SAMURAI

Full 3D Japanese Crafting @COMMENT_BODY@ Business Simulation

Create a beautiful, immersive 3D Japanese-inspired life simulation and business management game.

You play as a samurai who has left warfare behind to live peacefully in the Japanese mountains. Your goal is to build a successful estate through bonsai cultivation, gardening, traditional weapon crafting and trading.

1. YOUR ESTATE @COMMENT_BODY@ BONSAI GARDEN

Start with a small traditional Japanese house, a garden and a basic workshop.

Grow and cultivate different trees and flowers, including Japanese maple, cherry blossom, juniper, pine and bamboo.

Create and maintain beautiful bonsai through watering, pruning, wiring, shaping and repotting. Each tree has its own age, health, rarity, appearance and value.

Living Bonsai Legacy: Trees grow and develop over time. Rare trees can take years in-game to become masterpieces worth enormous amounts of money. Players can sell them at auctions or preserve them as family heirlooms and centrepieces of their estate.

Expand your garden with ponds, bridges, stone lanterns, decorative paths and traditional Japanese architecture.

2. BLACKSMITHING @COMMENT_BODY@ WEAPON CRAFTING

Build and upgrade a traditional Japanese blacksmith workshop.

Craft:

- Katana, Wakizashi, Tanto and Nodachi.
- Sai, Kunai and Naginata.
- Spears, bows and other traditional weapons.
- Samurai armour and decorative accessories.

Include interactive crafting stages such as heating, hammering, folding steel, sharpening, polishing and decorating.

Weapons have individual quality, materials, durability, rarity, appearance and value.

Legendary Weapons: Discover extremely rare materials and unlock secret crafting techniques to create unique legendary weapons. These creations attract wealthy samurai, collectors and supernatural buyers.

3. THE MOUNTAIN AUCTION

Create a beautiful Japanese mountain marketplace where players sell their bonsai, weapons and crafted goods.

Different NPC buyers include:

- Samurai looking for exceptional weapons.
- Buddhist monks collecting rare bonsai.
- Wealthy merchants seeking valuable items.
- Nobles collecting luxury decorations.
- Oni interested in mysterious and legendary creations.

Implement a proper auction system with starting bids, competing buyers, bidding wars, negotiations, seasonal demand and special auctions.

Different buyers have different preferences and budgets. Every item should have its own market value.

4. THE SECRET ONI BLACK MARKET

Introduce a mysterious underground auction that only appears at night.

Oni and supernatural merchants trade unusual and forbidden items.

Discover:

- Enchanted metals.
- Ancient seeds.
- Rare supernatural wood.
- Mysterious bonsai species.
- Forbidden weapon blueprints.
- Legendary crafting materials.

These items allow players to create extraordinary bonsai and weapons that cannot be produced through normal crafting.

The Oni market should be mysterious, rare and rewarding, adding fantasy elements without turning the peaceful game into a combat game.

5. ECONOMY @COMMENT_BODY@ PROGRESSION

Earn money through auctions and use it to:

- Purchase better materials and rare seeds.
- Upgrade workshops and equipment.
- Expand your property.
- Unlock new bonsai species and weapon designs.
- Hire gardeners and blacksmith assistants.
- Discover advanced crafting techniques.

Start as an unknown craftsman and gradually become one of Japan's most respected artisans.

Include reputation, customer relationships, rare commissions and increasingly wealthy buyers.

6. WORLD @COMMENT_BODY@ ENVIRONMENT

Create an explorable Japanese mountain environment containing:

- Bamboo forests.
- Cherry blossom valleys.
- Ancient temples and shrines.
- Mountain waterfalls and rivers.
- Mining caves.
- Traditional Japanese villages.
- Merchant settlements.
- The mountain auction grounds.

Include a complete seasonal system:
Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter.

Seasons, weather and time should influence bonsai growth, market demand and the appearance of the world.

7. VISUALS @COMMENT_BODY@ GAMEPLAY

Fully 3D, beautiful Japanese-inspired graphics with detailed environments, realistic crafting animations, dynamic lighting, day/night cycles and peaceful traditional Japanese-inspired music.

The game should be relaxing, rewarding and immersive.

CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP

GROW BONSAI → CRAFT WEAPONS → DISCOVER RARE MATERIALS → SELL AT AUCTION → EARN MONEY → UPGRADE YOUR ESTATE → CREATE LEGENDARY MASTERPIECES.

IMPORTANT: Prioritise fully functional gameplay systems over decorative features. Bonsai cultivation, weapon crafting, auctions, the economy and estate progression must all be playable and interconnected.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
We need to build a complete 3D game from scratch. Static HTML + Three.js. Since it's a static html project, we can use a CDN for three.js? Network may be blocked in preview? Better to vendor three.js locally. Let me check if network access available and whether npm install three works. Vite project may complicate build; simplest: package.json with vite + three, and use static deployment. But dependency install at start... start.sh uses default-start.mjs which handles vite. Capture uses playwright likely.

Let's check playwright-cli availability, node version, network.

Plan: build a single-page Three.js game with:

- 3D estate scene with Japanese house, garden, pond, bridge, lanterns, bonsai trees, workshop forge, mountains, torii, cherry trees, bamboo, snow seasons, day/night.
- UI overlay panels for Estate, Bonsai, Forge, Auction, Oni Market, World map/exploration, progression, employees.
- Game systems: trees with species, age, health, growth, styling (water, prune, wire, repot), value; weapons with types, materials, quality stages minigame (heat/hammer/fold/sharpen/polish via click timing), value; auction with NPC bidders and live bidding simulated; items market value; reputation, season, time, weather; oni black market at night; upgrades (workshop tiers, garden expansion, assistants); seeds/materials purchases; commissions.
- Sound: procedural shamisen/koto ambient with WebAudio (relaxing Japanese-inspired), wind, forge, water.
- Save/load via localStorage.
- Controls: orbit camera, click objects to focus, WASD? Simpler: click scene markers + camera orbit. Mobile responsive.

Need quality visuals. Build entire thing from scratch with custom geometry. No external assets (procedural textures via canvas). Three.js vendor.

Architecture: modular JS files? Simpler to do a few modules: main.js, world.js, bonsai.js, crafting.js, auction.js, ui.js, audio.js, state.js. Use Vite for bundling with three dependency. Let's set up package.json with vite and three. Npm install may be available. Check.

Let me test network and playwright.

- Build a complete, playable 3D Japanese-inspired life and business simulation titled “THE WAY OF THE SAMURAI.”

## Requirements
- Implement interconnected gameplay for bonsai cultivation, weapon crafting, auctions, economy, and estate progression.
- Include seasonal mountain environments, day/night cycles, varied NPC buyers, and a night-only supernatural Oni market.
- Prioritize functional gameplay over decorative features; support responsive mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide); read only the latest screenshot.

- No implementation decisions made.

- Inspected the repository; found no existing game source files or `package.json`.

### Active
- Begin implementing the game in the currently bare project.

- (none)

1. Inspect available project scripts and runtime support, then create the game implementation.
2. Run the project and verify gameplay and visuals; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

- (none)

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser

  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element

  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)

  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`

  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file

## The Way of the Samurai — complete

The game is implemented and playable at `http://localhost:3002` (dev) and `http://localhost:3000` (production build).

### What's in it
- **Bonsai cultivation** — plant, water, prune, wire, fertilize, repot, rename, set heirlooms; trees age, grow, gain style, and change value.
- **Weapon forging** — six-stage timing minigame (heat, hammer, fold, sharpen, polish, decorate), material tiers, blueprints, quality/durability, legendary and supernatural blades.
- **Live auctions** — seasonal demand, appraisal, three opening-bid strategies, animated rival buyers, early hammer, fees, payouts, reputation, and result actions.
- **Economy & estate** — village market, commissions and patrons, garden/workshop upgrades, staff wages, decor, visitor income, temple blessings, gathering nodes, focused-work actions.
- **World** — seasonal mountain estate (spring/summer/autumn/winter), day/night lighting, weather, third-person movement, NPCs, koi pond, forge smoke, waterfall, bamboo forest, village, temple, auction grounds, cherry grove, mine.
- **Oni night market** — accessible only after nightfall at the red gate; rotating forbidden wares, nightly auction lot, rival Oni bidding, blueprints, enchanted steel and supernatural trees.
- **Persistence** — autosave to localStorage, save-on-rest, and a working “Begin again” reset.
- **Controls** — WASD/arrows, drag to orbit, scroll/pinch to zoom, E to interact, M for map, Esc to close; mobile joystick, drag, pinch, and interact button.

### Verification
- `npm run build` passes; production bundle served and launched successfully.
- Tested in Chromium at **1280×800** and **390×844**: intro/start, movement and joystick, every panel, watering/shaping, a full forge run (81-quality tantō), a live auction sale and payout, Oni lot bidding through a win, resting and day advance, upgrades/hiring/decor/gathering/blessing, and the reset flow.
- Panels and footers fit both desktop and mobile without horizontal overflow; camera collision and spawn framing were fixed.

### Assumptions
- Single-player browser game, WebGL required; all models, textures, and audio are procedural.
- Auctions resolve automatically as rival bidders drop out; “Bring down the hammer” sells early.
- The Oni gate only opens at night; its stock and lot change each day.
- There is no hard ending — progression is measured by rank, reputation, quests, masterpieces, and estate growth.
- Progress lives in localStorage; “Begin again” permanently clears it.

The generated `dist/` build is up to date with the source.
